chunks: It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Indeed, I have been afflicted with this knowledge. I intend a need, and when I look at the ascendant and see the ascendant as evil, I sit and do not go regarding it; and when I see the ascendant as good, I go regarding the need.”
So he said to me: “Do you get it done?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Burn your books.”

key_terms.ابْتُلِيتُ: I have been afflicted or tested
key_terms.الطَّالِعِ: the ascendant or rising sign observed for omens
key_terms.الْحَاجَةِ: the need or matter one intends to pursue
key_terms.الْعِلْمِ: the knowledge being referred to here, namely astrological knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about acting on astrology when deciding whether to pursue one’s affairs?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a man informing Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he relied on astrological indications before pursuing his affairs. When the Imam عليه السلام learned that he acted upon this practice, he instructed him to burn his books, indicating rejection of reliance on such knowledge in conduct.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2402 - It is narrated from Abdul Malik ibn A'yan who said:
"I said to Abu Abdullah (as) 'I have been tested with this knowledge (of astrology). When I intend to fulfill a need and observe the rising star, if I see it as unfavorable, I sit and do not proceed. But if I see it as favorable, I proceed with my need.'
Imam (as) said to me: 'Do you accomplish it?'
I said: 'Yes.'
Imam (as) said: 'Burn your books.'"
